Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
The stomach-churning selloff that rocked equities has options traders girding for more volatility ahead.
Stocks have been increasingly turbulent in recent weeks, roiled by concerns ranging from higher interest rates to a Democratic sweep in US midterm elections that may change the regulatory landscape for artificial intelligence-focused firms. To derivatives strategists, the pattern pointed to an increase in so-called fragility — a condition where long periods of calm are broken up by oversized market swings.

A heavy storm that hit Brazil’s southern state of Rio Grande do Sul on Friday devastated a small town and raised concerns that continued rains and strong winds may bring further damage to crucial agriculture areas.
Brazil’s federal government recognized a state of public calamity in Tupanciretã, a town of about 20,000 people some 1,000 km southwest of Sao Paulo, and the surrounding region. The town’s government declared 100% of the municipality’s area affected by the storm.

IQVIA Holdings Inc. is closing in on a roughly $1.1 billion takeover of Quotient Sciences, as the US clinical research group looks to expand its role in bringing new medicines to market.
A deal for the Nottingham, UK-based drug development and manufacturing specialist could be announced as soon as Monday, barring any last-minute snags, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: GTA VI Takes Over Thanksgiving Week
item.description:
Nov 22nd, 2026
GTA VI Takes Over Thanksgiving Week
On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg reporter Josyana Joshua tells host Lisa Mateo how the long-awaited release of Grand Theft Auto VI is becoming a cultural and workplace phenomenon, with gamers taking time off and preparing to play through Thanksgiving week. Joshua explains how the game’s 13-year buildup is driving demand for consoles and gaming gear while potentially competing with family gatherings, football and other holiday entertainment.

item.title: Fed’s Inflation Fight May Require More Hikes
item.description:
Nov 22nd, 2026
Fed’s Inflation Fight May Require More Hikes
Neil Dutta, head of US economic research at Renaissance Macro Research, tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the Federal Reserve made a mistake by holding rates steady in October and may need multiple hikes as inflation remains stubbornly above its 2% target. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Dutta says the recent market selloff does not yet signal broader economic trouble, arguing that AI investment and a resilient labor market continue to support growth even as the Fed has less flexibility to cushion falling markets.

item.title: Governors Push States to Lead on AI
item.description:
Bloomberg This Weekend • Nov 22nd, 2026
Governors Push States to Lead on AI
On Bloomberg This Weekend, Governors Wes Moore, Spencer Cox, Josh Stein and Mike Braun tell host Christina Ruffini that states need to take a larger role in shaping AI and data center policy as concerns grow over electricity costs, water use, jobs and consumer protections. The bipartisan group says data centers should largely pay for their own energy needs and emphasizes local control, while differing over how aggressively the federal government should regulate AI.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
For years, a strong earnings season has given Wall Street something to fall back on. But the crumbling artificial-intelligence trade has ripped away that support.
Companies in the S&P 500 Index just delivered a second-consecutive quarter of profit growth in excess of 30%, defying fears rising costs would slow earnings. Instead of rallying, the index slumped, signaling strong results alone aren’t enough to protect mounting anxiety around the AI trade.

Save
Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Fuel subsidies are driving a widening divide in emerging markets, with investors favoring bonds from nations that have taken the painful steps to curb them.
In Bolivia, a decision to end a government program that kept diesel prices artificially low has helped ease pressure on public finances and hand investors over 7% returns on its dollar bonds this year, the most in Latin America. Oil-exporter Angola, meanwhile, has struggled to reap the full benefits of higher crude prices as soaring costs for imported refined fuels eat into government finances.

item.title: Trump’s Asia Trip Leaves Key Issues Unresolved
item.description: ABC News State Department reporter Shannon Kingston tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Russia’s increasingly provocative actions near NATO countries are complicating President Donald Trump’s push for a negotiated end to the war in Ukraine, while Moscow remains publicly defiant. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Kingston says Trump’s Asia trip produced few concrete results and puts greater pressure on the upcoming G20 meetings to deliver progress on China, trade and other unresolved diplomatic issues. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Taiwan Mulls Lowering Margin Requirement to Support Stock Market
item.description: Taiwan is considering lowering the margin requirement ratio for stock investors using borrowed funds as it tries to stem a selloff after the benchmark equity index’s worst week in 35 years.

item.title: Asia’s Stock Rescue Efforts Gather Pace After Wall Street Plunge
item.description: Asian authorities are stepping up efforts to stem a deepening stock-market rout, with China easing margin requirements, and Taiwan and South Korea rolling out intervention measures following Friday’s plunge in US equities.

item.title: US Power Advantage Over China Shrinks Further on Iran War Effect
item.description: The advantage the US has over China in influencing the course of international events has shrunk to the smallest level since 2018, with the Iran war and unilateralism undermining its military and diplomatic strength, according to a new report.

item.title: From Squeezes to Meltdown, a Week of Mayhem Rocks Metals Markets
item.description: As the copper industry gathered in Shanghai last week, Grace Li was struck by the overwhelmingly bearish mood over the outlook for demand. She agreed with the pessimism. In fact, she came close to pulling out her phone on the spot to put on a short position after her Monday conversations.
